officials.bio: Commissioner Jack Manning began working in the Pittsburgh region in 1998 and relocated to the Chippewa Township / Beaver Falls area in 2000. He was sworn into office for his first term in January 2020 and re-elected for a second term starting in January 2024. Prior to his commissionership, Jack owned Pinebrook Cottage Consulting (PCC) after a 35-year career in the Petro-chemical industry.

officials.name: Kimberly D. Geyer
officials.bio: Kimberly Geyer is a 1984 graduate of Butler County Community College and a former business owner. She served on the Mars School Board for twelve years and began her third term as a Butler County Commissioner in 2016. She is actively involved in various county and state-level boards and committees.

officials.name: Max R. Pavlovich
officials.bio: Max R. Pavlovich is currently serving his second term as Cambria County’s Clerk of Courts. Max is a lifelong Cambria County resident and a graduate of the University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown. After graduation, Max was hired by the Pennsylvania House of Representatives as a legislative assistant, helping residents solve their state related issues. Later, Max moved into the private side of healthcare, operating as Administrator for a personal care facility.

officials.name: Ray D'Agostino
officials.address: 150 N. Queen St. Seventh Floor, Suite 715 Lancaster, PA 17603
officials.hours: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p. m.
officials.bio: Ray D’Agostino was first elected as a Lancaster County Commissioner in 2019 and re-elected in 2023. Previous to this post he served for ten years as CEO of the Lancaster Housing Opportunity Partnership (LHOP), a regional U.S. Treasury certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) that was focused on housing affordability. Ray also served as the first Chief of Staff for former State Senator Smucker (now Congressman) and spent 17 years in local government as a municipal and authority manager.

officials.name: Alice Yoder
officials.address: 150 N. Queen St. Seventh Floor, Suite 715 Lancaster, PA 17603
officials.hours: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p. m.
officials.bio: Alice Yoder was elected to the Lancaster County Board of Commissioners in 2023. She began her professional career as a critical care registered nurse and later developed the Wellness Center at Lancaster General Health, focusing on health promotion and disease prevention. She has also served on various planning commissions and boards, driven by a desire to improve lives for all people in Lancaster County.

officials.name: Joshua Parsons
officials.address: 150 N. Queen St. Seventh Floor, Suite 715 Lancaster, PA 17603
officials.hours: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p. m.
officials.bio: Josh Parsons has served as an Army infantry officer, prosecutor, and no-nonsense conservative executive. He has delivered on promises to fight crime and run an efficient county government that sets conditions for working people and families to thrive here in Lancaster County. In November 2023, he was reelected as County Commissioner, earning more votes than any commissioner candidate in Lancaster County history.

officials.name: Joseph M. Klebon
officials.bio: Joe is a lifelong resident of the County having grown up in the Shamokin – Coal Township area. He graduated from Shamokin Area High School in 1972 and is a 1976 graduate of Lycoming College where he was a member of the football team. He furthered his education receiving graduate degrees from both Bucknell University with a Master of Science in Education and Indiana University of Pennsylvania, with a degree in Administration.

officials.name: Meghan K. Beck
officials.bio: Meghan K. Beck is a local entrepreneur and community volunteer, and a long-time resident of Northumberland County. A Bucknell University graduate with a BA in Political Science, she is a partner in 1337 Rentals and the Sunbury Market House, and founder of STEAM Innovation Labs. She is dedicated to community development, helping small businesses, and actively volunteers for various local initiatives.

officials.name: Samuel J. Schiccatano
officials.bio: Sam, a lifelong resident of Northumberland County, graduated from Shamokin Area High School in 1972 and earned a degree in Sociology and Elementary Education from Lycoming College in 1976. He taught for 36 years at the Shamokin Area School District, where he also served as the PSEA Teachers Union President for six years.

officials.name: Cherelle L. Parker
officials.bio: بالاعتماد على أكثر من ثلاثة عقود من الخدمة العامة، تتميز مسيرة العمدة شيريل إل باركر المهنية بالتزامها العميق تجاه مدينة فيلادلفيا. إن رحلتها من متدربة في المدرسة الثانوية في مجلس المدينة إلى أعلى منصب في المدينة هي شهادة على تفانيها وقيادتها.

officials.name: Cherelle L. Parker
officials.bio: في 2 يناير 2024، تم تنصيب شيريل باركر كعمدة رقم 100 لفيلادلفيا، لتصبح أول امرأة تقود المدينة وتتولى المنصب منذ 341 عامًا. العمدة باركر هي معلمة سابقة في مدرسة عامة، ومشرعة الولاية التي ترأست وفد فيلادلفيا، وعضو مجلس مدينة فيلادلفيا، حيث مثلت المقاطعة التاسعة وترقت لتصبح زعيمة الأغلبية. بصفتها فيلادلفية مدى الحياة، فهي ملتزمة بالقتال كل يوم من أجل سكان فيلادلفيا.

officials.name: Paige G. Cognetti
officials.bio: Mayor Cognetti was sworn in as Mayor of Scranton on January 6, 2020, and won re-election to a full term in November 2021. Prior to becoming Mayor, she advised the Pennsylvania Auditor General and served on the Scranton School Board. She also served in the Obama administration as a senior advisor at the U.S. Treasury Department.

officials.name: Scott Burford
officials.hours: Monday through Friday 8 AM to 4:30 PM
officials.bio: Scott has more than 32 years of experience in both private and public sectors. Prior to his election as York County Commissioner, he served as the Chief Clerk/Chief of Staff for the Dauphin County Commissioners and as the Chairman of the Springettsbury Township Board of Auditors. In the private sector, Scott spent 15 years in health services administration, holding a license as a Nursing Home Administrator in PA, WV, and VA.

officials.name: Edquina Washington
officials.bio: Edquina Washington, a Democrat, was appointed to York City Council on January 24, 2018, to fill a vacancy and served until the first Monday of January 2020. After a successful election bid, Edquina was elected to York City Council in January 2020 to serve a four-year term and was again reelected in January 2024 to a four-year term. Edquina serves as Council’s liaison to the City/School District Cooperation & Open Communications Committee, York City Civil Service Board, and the York City Housing Authority Board.

officials.name: Sandie Walker
officials.bio: Sandie Denise Walker was first elected as York City Mayor in November 2025. A graduate of William Penn Senior High School and the University of Richmond, she began her career in public service with the York City Health Bureau and as Youth Program Coordinator. She previously served six years as a director for the School District of the City of York and as President of York City Council.
